name: GM Fast Film Glow

name: GM Film Grunge / Damage
desc: Authentic dust, hairs, scratches, grain, projector flicker and gate weave in one film pass.

name: GM Flashback
desc: A complete memory-sequence treatment in one effect. Five stock looks - sepia memory, bleach bypass, warm nostalgia, cold memory and faded print - set the base grade, then a real bright-pass bloom, film flicker, gate weave jitter, emulsion grain, vertical scratches, dust, a soft vignette, a directional light leak and a frame-step stutter are layered on top. Every one of those is its own control, so the same effect can be a clean sepia wash or a badly kept reel. Grade, grain, weave and bloom are all measured in layer space, so the treatment travels with the layer.

name: GM Flow Smear
desc: Image-gradient-driven paint flow that follows local contours instead of using a fixed blur direction.
shader: float l(vec2 p){return dot(texture2DCv(inputImg.texture,clamp(p,0.0,1.0)).rgb,vec3(.2126,.7152,.0722));}void main(){vec2 uv=acScreenNorm,sz=max(inputImg.size,vec2(1.0)),e=1.0/sz;vec4 src=texture2DCv(inputImg.texture,uv);vec2 grad=vec2(l(uv+vec2(e.x,0))-l(uv-vec2(e.x,0)),l(uv+vec2(0,e.y))-l(uv-vec2(0,e.y)));float edge=length(grad);vec2 dir=normalize(vec2(-grad.y,grad.x)+vec2(.0001));vec4 sum=vec4(0);float ws=0.0,count=clamp(floor(samples+.5),4.0,24.0);for(int i=0;i<24;i++){if(float(i)>=count)break;float t=float(i)/max(count-1.0,1.0)-.5;vec2 bend=vec2(-dir.y,dir.x)*curvature*t*t;float w=1.0-abs(t);sum+=texture2DCv(inputImg.texture,clamp(uv+(dir*t+bend)*lengthPx/sz,0.0,1.0))*w;ws+=w;}float mask=smoothstep(edgeThreshold,edgeThreshold*3.0+.001,edge)*(1.0-detail);gl_FragColor=mix(src,sum/max(ws,.001),mixAmount*mask);}

name: GM Gradient Map
desc: A four-stop colour ramp mapped onto any channel of the layer. Pick what drives the ramp - luminance, a single channel, alpha, hue, saturation or lightness - then set the four colours and where the two middle stops sit. The ramp can be interpolated in RGB, in HSV (shortest hue path, so a red-to-blue ramp goes through magenta rather than through grey) or in luma-preserved mode, which keeps the layer's own brightness and takes only the ramp's colour. A bias curve, a contrast curve, dithering and five blend modes finish it. Layer space, so the ramp rides the layer.

name: GM Gradient Ramp
desc: A positional three-colour ramp laid over the layer - linear at any angle, radial, angular, diamond, mirrored or procedural noise. The ramp runs through three stops with a movable midpoint and a softness control that goes from a hard three-colour band through to a fully smooth blend. The noise shape scrolls and scales, which turns the ramp into a drifting colour cloud. Five blend modes and an opacity control composite it back onto the source. Everything is measured in layer space, so the ramp is welded to the layer.

name: GM Granite
desc: Five stone surfaces generated in layer space. Granite builds crystalline cells from a cellular noise field and drops mineral speckle on top, Marble runs a turbulent sine through the field to make veins, Sandstone lays down horizontal sedimentary bands, Basalt grows columnar joints, and Concrete is an octave stack with grit. A real bump normal is taken from the pattern's own gradient and lit from an adjustable angle, so the surface has relief instead of being a flat texture. Pattern scale, octaves, crystal size, speckle, vein strength, roughness and a source modulation are all separate controls.

name: GM Height Map
desc: Treats the layer's luminance as a terrain height field and then renders that terrain six different ways. Shaded Relief lights it from an adjustable sun, Contour Lines draws isolines at a settable spacing, Emboss adds the relief back onto the original, Normal Map writes the surface normal as a colour, Displace actually pushes the layer's pixels along the slope, and Slate quantises the terrain into flat geological bands. Height scale, light angle and sun height, a pre-blur, and separate ink and paper colours. Measured in layer space, so the terrain is the layer's own.

name: GM Hue Shift Tunnel
desc: Wraps the layer around a tunnel and rotates the hue with depth, so the colour cycles as the corridor recedes. Five cross sections: a round bore, a square bore, a hexagonal kaleidoscopic bore, a triangular one, and a flat corridor. Depth scale, travel speed, hue per unit of depth, a global hue rotation, ring shading along the tunnel, a twist that skews the bore with distance, a swirl that rotates the whole wall, saturation and brightness are all separate. The tunnel centre is a layer point, so the whole corridor is welded to the layer.

name: GM Pixel Reveal
desc: Reveals or hides the layer through a pixel-block dissolve, and it is a real reveal - the unrevealed area is transparent, so whatever sits underneath shows through. Six orders: a random per-block dissolve, a directional block wipe, a mosaic that grows from a centre point, coarse random tiles, a checkerboard sweep, and fine scan lines. Progress is a manual control or can be animated on its own, block size and direction are independent, and randomness blends the wipe order between perfectly regular and completely scattered. There is an edge glow on the reveal frontier, a mosaic stage so the revealed area can pass through a pixelated look first, and a choice of what the hidden area shows. Layer space, so the blocks are cut from the layer.

name: GM Posterize
desc: Six different quantisers over one tone stage. Channel Levels clips each channel independently, Luma Bands keeps the hue and bands only the brightness, Ordered and Noise Dither dissolve the steps with a Bayer 8 lattice or a hash, Halftone Dots rebuilds the picture out of rotatable ink dots, and Riso Offset prints two shifted ink passes on top of each other. A duotone ramp can then map the result onto any two colours. Everything is built in LAYER space, so the pattern scales and rotates with the layer instead of sitting on the frame.

name: GM RGB Rainbow
desc: A full-spectrum rainbow generated from six different drivers: the layer's own luminance, a rotatable position axis, distance from a point, angle around a point, time, or a blend of luma and position. Hue range, cycles, phase and a separate hue shift let you dial in anything from a two-colour sweep to a tight prism band. The spectrum is then composited onto the source with a real blend mode. Built in layer space, so the gradient is part of the layer and moves with it.

name: GM Channel Swap
desc: Five ways to rearrange the colour channels. Rotate Cycles the channels round, Channel Mixer is a full 3x3 matrix so any output channel can be rebuilt from any mix of the inputs, Swap Pairs trades two channels at a time, Invert Mask flips any combination of R/G/B with a 3-bit mask, and Luma Split holds the brightness exactly and spins only the chroma through YCbCr. Runs on the layer's own pixels through the layer transform, so it keeps working when the layer is moved, scaled or rotated.

name: GM Color Swap
desc: Three independent find-and-replace slots. Each one matches a colour by RGB distance, hue or luminance, with its own tolerance and soft edge, and swaps it for whatever you pick - so you can repaint a whole grade by targeting three key colours. Hue Only keeps the original brightness and takes just the new hue, which is what stops a skin tone from turning into flat paint. A global saturation boost and a strength control sit on top. Layer space throughout, so the replacement travels with the layer.

name: GM Curve
desc: Bends the layer like a sheet of paper. The layer is treated as a real cylindrical surface: the coordinate along the bend axis is mapped through an arc, a perspective divide is applied so the far side genuinely foreshortens, and the perpendicular axis scales with it - which is why the result reads as a curved object instead of as a stretched picture. Six presets cover bowing inward, bowing outward, a flat arc, a full cylinder, an S-curve that reverses across the middle and a page curl. Bend amount, axis, curvature profile, perspective, anchor, twist, a directional sheen and clamp/mirror/wrap sampling are all separate.

name: GM Fluid Ink
desc: Second-order curl advection with controllable viscosity and two-color liquid ink shading.

name: GM Fluid Refraction Field

name: GM Timeslice Warp

Multiply Gain is the straight per-channel multiplier, Additive Offset adds a constant per channel, Screen blends the offset back so nothing clips, and Overlay Boost multiplies but soft-limits the top end so highlights roll off instead of flattening. Preserve Luma rescales the result so a channel-heavy grade does not change the overall brightness. Built in layer space, so the grade rides the layer.

name: GM Hue Shift Bands
desc: Hue rotation applied in discrete bands. The layer's luminance, a rotatable position axis, distance from a point, angle around a point or time is cut into N bands, and each band gets its own hue offset - so instead of one flat rotation you get a stepped rainbow that follows the picture. Bands can also drive a saturation and a brightness wave, the edges can be feathered so the steps read as a soft posterise rather than a hard cut, and the whole stack can scroll over time. The source is then pulled outward from every cell centre so the tissue bulges, and the whole field can breathe. Six presets: tissue, a vein-dominant network, a membrane-dominant skin, pulsing cells, an irregular fungal growth and an elongated sinew. Cell size, size variation, field complexity, distortion, pulse rate, vein width, vein glow, membrane strength, an organic colour shift and the cell and vein colours are all separate. Six behaviours: dissolve outward, rise, explode, swirl, fall, and orbit. Gravity, turbulence, a spread control, size variation, an anisotropic trail stretch, a soft glow halo, colour boost, a per-particle birth and death cycle and the lattice density are all independent. The lattice centre is a layer point, so the whole system rides the layer.

name: GM Text Cascade
desc: A time driven build-on and tear-down. Every character is given an ORDER KEY along the line, and the build progress sweeps those keys one after another - so the text assembles itself. Order can run Forward, Backward, start at the Center and work Out, start at the Edges and work In, go Random, or assemble Word by Word. Stagger sets how far apart the characters are; at zero the whole line lands together, at maximum it becomes a long per-character cascade. Three reveal styles: Typewriter simply withholds the character, Placeholder Wipe parks a chosen glyph in its slot so the layout never reflows, and Scramble boils unrevealed characters through a glyph pool. Reverse Out collapses the finished line again from the end, on its own clock, so one effect covers both the in and the out.

name: GM Text Case Wave
desc: A travelling wave of typography. A sine wave is laid along the line and wherever its crest passes, the characters change - they can invert their current case, force caps, force lower case, alternate one by one, randomise, double themselves, or dissolve into blank space. The wave is a function of the character's position along the line AND of time, so it genuinely travels. Direction picks the spatial coordinate: Forward and Backward run the crest end to end, Center Out starts at the middle and sweeps both ways, Edges In does the reverse, and Random hashes each character so the change boils instead of sweeping. Band Width sets how many characters are caught at once and Band Sharpness decides whether the band has soft shoulders or hard ones.

name: GM Text Glitch
desc: A bursty corruption, not a constant noise. A burst clock decides WHEN the text is attacked; between bursts the text is untouched. Inside a burst four independent strikes fire on their own hashed blocks: whole blocks of characters are displaced (the sliced-and-reglued datamosh look), individual glyphs are swapped for a chosen pool, characters stutter by repeating themselves, and characters drop out entirely. Every strike is hashed from the burst index, so no two bursts are alike, and nothing is random - a preview and an export produce exactly the same frames. The clock runs on the LAYER's own time, so the corruption travels with the layer.

name: GM Text Marquee
desc: An endless ticker. The line is joined into a ring with a gap of your choosing and then scrolled through a fixed window, so the text never runs out and never jumps - it wraps seamlessly. Three motion modes: Loop runs the ring forever, Ping-Pong runs it out and brings it back, and Reveal Once travels a single pass then holds at the far end. The window is a fraction of the original line, the anchor decides where the window sits inside the frame, and the whole thing can run on the layer's own clock or on absolute timeline time so several tickers can share one scroll.

name: GM Time Slice
desc: Cuts the layer into bands and gives each band its own moment. Six constructions: Slit Scan slides every band sideways by a progressively larger amount, Repeat Tile replaces each band's slice coordinate with its own so the picture tiles along the axis, Mirror Echo reflects it about the band centre for a kaleidoscopic echo, Radial Slices does the same thing in polar coordinates, Stretch Bands scales each band around its own centre, and Freeze Column makes every band take its content from the first. Band count, offset, an accumulation curve, stagger, edge feather, direction, animation, in-band blur and clamp/mirror/wrap sampling are all separate.

name: GM Twirl
desc: A twirl with real structure. The twist profile is a power curve over the radius, so the falloff control moves the effect from a tight knot at the centre to a wide slow rotation that reaches the edge. Six looks: a plain twirl, a whirlpool that also scales with the twist, a spiral that couples the radius to the angle, a pinch twirl, a black hole that pulls inward and darkens the core, and a double twirl whose two lobes counter-rotate. Ring ripple, turbulence, spin, and clamp/mirror/wrap sampling are all separate controls. Measured in layer space around a layer point.

name: GM Text Animator
desc: A real per-character text animator running inside the native glyph engine. Every character (or word, or line) is given its own 0 to 1 progress and that progress is pushed through the animation CURVE you choose from the Animation Type dropdown. Because the curve is evaluated per component you get staggered, springy, overshooting and bouncing motion from a single effect - no expression graph, no elastic setup, no manual keyframing. Bounce In drops the line in and lets each character settle with decaying bounces; Bounce Out tears it away; Elastic and Spring wobble; Back overshoots once; Wave and Pulse keep moving forever; Smooth Settle and Expo Snap give clean professional landings. Offset, Angle, Scale, Stretch and Alpha are the AMPLITUDE of the motion - the curve only decides HOW the component travels along it. Frequency sets how many bounces or wobbles happen, Damping how fast they die out, Overshoot how hard they hit. Apply To switches the whole animator between letters, words, lines or the whole block.

const vec3 L=vec3(0.2126,0.7152,0.0722);vec3 pnkjStreakHighlight(vec4 c){float y=dot(c.rgb,L);return c.rgb*max(y-threshold,0.0)/max(y,0.0001);}
void main(){vec2 uv=acScreenNorm;vec2 texSize=max(inputImg.size,vec2(1.0));vec2 p=vec2(length/texSize.x,0.0);vec4 s=texture2DCv(inputImg.texture,uv);vec3 v=pnkjStreakHighlight(s)*0.20;v+=(pnkjStreakHighlight(texture2DCv(inputImg.texture,clamp(uv+p*0.25,0.0,1.0)))+pnkjStreakHighlight(texture2DCv(inputImg.texture,clamp(uv-p*0.25,0.0,1.0))))*0.16;v+=(pnkjStreakHighlight(texture2DCv(inputImg.texture,clamp(uv+p*0.5,0.0,1.0)))+pnkjStreakHighlight(texture2DCv(inputImg.texture,clamp(uv-p*0.5,0.0,1.0))))*0.12;v+=(pnkjStreakHighlight(texture2DCv(inputImg.texture,clamp(uv+p,0.0,1.0)))+pnkjStreakHighlight(texture2DCv(inputImg.texture,clamp(uv-p,0.0,1.0))))*0.08;gl_FragColor=vec4(s.rgb+v*tint.rgb*strength,s.a);}

name: GM Chromatic Grain
desc: Luma-aware RGB film grain with stable per-channel sampling.
shader: float pnkjRand(vec2 p){return fract(sin(dot(p,vec2(12.9898,78.233)))*43758.5453);}void main(){vec2 u=acScreenNorm;vec4 s=texture2DCv(inputImg.texture,u);vec2 texSize=max(inputImg.size,vec2(1.0));vec2 p=floor(u*texSize/max(size,0.5))+floor(phase);float g=pnkjRand(p)-0.5;vec3 cg=vec3(pnkjRand(p+1.7),pnkjRand(p+8.3),pnkjRand(p+19.1))-0.5;float l=1.0-0.55*dot(s.rgb,vec3(0.2126,0.7152,0.0722));vec3 noise=mix(vec3(g),cg,clamp(chroma,0.0,1.0))*amount*l;gl_FragColor=vec4(clamp(s.rgb+noise,0.0,1.0),s.a);}

name: GM Directional Echo
desc: Weighted temporal-style directional image echoes with smooth attenuation.
shader: void main(){vec2 u=acScreenNorm;vec2 texSize=max(inputImg.size,vec2(1.0));vec2 d=vec2(cos(angle),sin(angle))*distance/texSize;vec4 s=texture2DCv(inputImg.texture,u);vec4 q=vec4(0.0);float w=1.0;float z=0.0;for(int i=0;i<10;i++){float t=float(i)/9.0;q+=texture2DCv(inputImg.texture,clamp(u-d*t,0.0,1.0))*w;z+=w;w*=decay;}q/=max(z,0.0001);gl_FragColor=mix(s,q,clamp(mixAmount,0.0,1.0));}

name: GM Edge Luminescence
desc: Sobel-derived luminous edges composited over the original layer.
shader: const vec3 L=vec3(0.2126,0.7152,0.0722);float pnkjEdgeLuma(vec2 u){return dot(texture2DCv(inputImg.texture,clamp(u,0.0,1.0)).rgb,L);}void main(){vec2 u=acScreenNorm;vec2 p=width/max(inputImg.size,vec2(1.0));vec4 s=texture2DCv(inputImg.texture,u);float gx=-pnkjEdgeLuma(u-p)+pnkjEdgeLuma(u+vec2(p.x,-p.y))-2.0*pnkjEdgeLuma(u-vec2(p.x,0.0))+2.0*pnkjEdgeLuma(u+vec2(p.x,0.0))-pnkjEdgeLuma(u+vec2(-p.x,p.y))+pnkjEdgeLuma(u+p);float gy=-pnkjEdgeLuma(u-p)-2.0*pnkjEdgeLuma(u-vec2(0.0,p.y))-pnkjEdgeLuma(u+vec2(p.x,-p.y))+pnkjEdgeLuma(u+vec2(-p.x,p.y))+2.0*pnkjEdgeLuma(u+vec2(0.0,p.y))+pnkjEdgeLuma(u+p);float e=smoothstep(threshold,threshold+0.2,length(vec2(gx,gy)));gl_FragColor=vec4(s.rgb+edgeColor.rgb*e*strength,s.a);}

name: GM Emulsion Halation
desc: Warm film-stock highlight bleed driven by luminance rather than alpha.
shader:
const vec3 L=vec3(0.2126,0.7152,0.0722); float hi(vec4 c){return smoothstep(threshold,threshold+0.25,dot(c.rgb,L));}
void main(){vec2 uv=acScreenNorm;vec2 p=radius/inputImg.size;vec4 s=texture2DCv(inputImg.texture,uv);float h=0.18*hi(s);h+=0.1025*(hi(texture2DCv(inputImg.texture,uv+vec2(p.x,0.0)))+hi(texture2DCv(inputImg.texture,uv-vec2(p.x,0.0)))+hi(texture2DCv(inputImg.texture,uv+vec2(0.0,p.y)))+hi(texture2DCv(inputImg.texture,uv-vec2(0.0,p.y))));h+=0.1025*(hi(texture2DCv(inputImg.texture,uv+p))+hi(texture2DCv(inputImg.texture,uv-p))+hi(texture2DCv(inputImg.texture,uv+vec2(p.x,-p.y)))+hi(texture2DCv(inputImg.texture,uv+vec2(-p.x,p.y))));gl_FragColor=vec4(s.rgb+tint.rgb*h*strength,s.a);}

name: GM Highlight Recovery
desc: Reconstructs clipped highlights using local chroma and a smooth luminance shoulder.
shader: const vec3 L=vec3(0.2126,0.7152,0.0722);void main(){vec4 s=texture2DCv(inputImg.texture,acScreenNorm);float y=dot(s.rgb,L);float m=smoothstep(threshold,1.0,y);float compressed=threshold+(1.0-threshold)*(1.0-exp(-(max(y-threshold,0.0))/max(1.0-threshold,0.0001)));vec3 chroma=s.rgb/max(y,0.0001);vec3 rec=mix(vec3(compressed),chroma*compressed,chromaPreserve);gl_FragColor=vec4(mix(s.rgb,rec,m*amount),s.a);}

name: GM Luma Radiance
desc: Energy-preserving luminance aura with controllable threshold and color.
shader:
const vec3 L=vec3(0.2126,0.7152,0.0722);float pnkjRadianceEnergy(vec2 u){vec4 c=texture2DCv(inputImg.texture,clamp(u,0.0,1.0));return max(dot(c.rgb,L)-threshold,0.0);}
void main(){vec2 u=acScreenNorm;vec2 p=spread/max(inputImg.size,vec2(1.0));vec4 s=texture2DCv(inputImg.texture,u);float a=pnkjRadianceEnergy(u)*0.2;a+=(pnkjRadianceEnergy(u+vec2(p.x,0.0))+pnkjRadianceEnergy(u-vec2(p.x,0.0))+pnkjRadianceEnergy(u+vec2(0.0,p.y))+pnkjRadianceEnergy(u-vec2(0.0,p.y)))*0.12;a+=(pnkjRadianceEnergy(u+p)+pnkjRadianceEnergy(u-p)+pnkjRadianceEnergy(u+vec2(p.x,-p.y))+pnkjRadianceEnergy(u+vec2(-p.x,p.y)))*0.08;gl_FragColor=vec4(s.rgb+radianceColor.rgb*a*gain,s.a);}

name: GM Optical Diffusion
desc: Fine highlight diffusion that retains low-frequency contrast.
shader: const vec3 L=vec3(0.2126,0.7152,0.0722);void main(){vec2 uv=acScreenNorm;vec2 texSize=max(inputImg.size,vec2(1.0));vec2 p=radius/texSize;vec4 s=texture2DCv(inputImg.texture,uv);vec3 b=s.rgb*0.25;b+=(texture2DCv(inputImg.texture,clamp(uv+p,0.0,1.0)).rgb+texture2DCv(inputImg.texture,clamp(uv-p,0.0,1.0)).rgb+texture2DCv(inputImg.texture,clamp(uv+vec2(p.x,-p.y),0.0,1.0)).rgb+texture2DCv(inputImg.texture,clamp(uv+vec2(-p.x,p.y),0.0,1.0)).rgb)*0.1875;float y=dot(s.rgb,L);float m=clamp(mixAmount,0.0,1.0)*mix(1.0,smoothstep(0.15,1.0,y),clamp(highlightBias,0.0,1.0));gl_FragColor=vec4(mix(s.rgb,b,clamp(m,0.0,1.0)),s.a);}

name: GM Pixel Drift
desc: Block-coherent digital displacement with deterministic animated phase control.
shader: float pnkjPixelRand(vec2 p){return fract(sin(dot(p,vec2(12.9898,78.233)))*43758.5453);}void main(){vec2 u=acScreenNorm;vec2 sz=max(inputImg.size,vec2(1.0));vec2 cell=floor(u*sz/max(blockSize,1.0));float a=pnkjPixelRand(cell+floor(phase));vec2 o=vec2((a-0.5)*2.0,pnkjPixelRand(cell+floor(phase)+19.7)-0.5)*distance/sz;vec4 s=texture2DCv(inputImg.texture,u);vec4 d=texture2DCv(inputImg.texture,clamp(u+o,0.0,1.0));gl_FragColor=mix(s,d,clamp(mixAmount,0.0,1.0));}

name: GM Prism Warp
desc: Angle-controlled refractive prism split with smooth radial masking.
shader: void main(){vec2 u=acScreenNorm;vec2 d=vec2(cos(angle),sin(angle));float m=smoothstep(0.0,max(softness,0.0001),abs(dot(u-vec2(0.5),vec2(-d.y,d.x))));vec2 o=d*amount*m;vec4 s=texture2DCv(inputImg.texture,u);vec4 r=texture2DCv(inputImg.texture,clamp(u+o*dispersion,0.0,1.0));vec4 b=texture2DCv(inputImg.texture,clamp(u-o*dispersion,0.0,1.0));gl_FragColor=vec4(r.r,s.g,b.b,s.a);}

name: GM Radial Velocity
desc: Center-origin velocity blur with normalized weighted sampling.
shader: void main(){vec2 u=acScreenNorm;vec2 screenSize=max(acScreenSize,vec2(1.0));vec2 c=(acLayerCenter+center)/screenSize;vec2 d=u-c;float a=strength*pow(max(length(d)*1.4142,0.00001),max(falloff,0.00001));vec4 sum=vec4(0.0);float wsum=0.0;for(int i=0;i<12;i++){float t=float(i)/11.0;float w=1.0-abs(t-0.5);sum+=texture2DCv(inputImg.texture,clamp(u-d*a*t,0.0,1.0))*w;wsum+=w;}gl_FragColor=sum/max(wsum,0.0001);}

name: GM Spectral Aberration
desc: Lens-space RGB dispersion with radial falloff and independent strength.
shader: void main(){vec2 uv=acScreenNorm;vec2 screenSize=max(acScreenSize,vec2(1.0));vec2 c=(acLayerCenter+center)/screenSize;vec2 d=uv-c;float dist=length(d);float radial=pow(max(dist,0.00001),max(falloff,0.00001));vec2 dir=d/max(dist,0.00001);vec2 o=dir*amount*radial;vec4 src=texture2DCv(inputImg.texture,uv);vec4 redSample=texture2DCv(inputImg.texture,clamp(uv+o,0.0,1.0));vec4 blueSample=texture2DCv(inputImg.texture,clamp(uv-o,0.0,1.0));gl_FragColor=vec4(redSample.r,src.g,blueSample.b,src.a);}

name: GM Tonal Compression
desc: Filmic toe and shoulder mapping with luminance-preserving saturation.
shader: const vec3 L=vec3(0.2126,0.7152,0.0722);void main(){vec4 s=texture2DCv(inputImg.texture,acScreenNorm);vec3 x=max(s.rgb*pow(2.0,exposure),vec3(0.0));x=(x*(1.0+shoulder*x))/(1.0+x*(1.0+shoulder*x));x=mix(x,smoothstep(vec3(0.0),vec3(1.0),x),toe);float y=dot(x,L);x=mix(vec3(y),x,saturation);gl_FragColor=vec4(clamp(x,0.0,1.0),s.a);}

name: GM Turbulent Glass
desc: Multi-octave procedural refraction for organic glass distortion.
shader:
float pnkjGlassHash(vec2 p){return fract(sin(dot(p,vec2(127.1,311.7)))*43758.5453);}float pnkjGlassNoise(vec2 p){vec2 i=floor(p),q=fract(p);q=q*q*(3.0-2.0*q);return mix(mix(pnkjGlassHash(i),pnkjGlassHash(i+vec2(1,0)),q.x),mix(pnkjGlassHash(i+vec2(0,1)),pnkjGlassHash(i+vec2(1,1)),q.x),q.y);}float pnkjGlassFbm(vec2 p){return pnkjGlassNoise(p)*0.6+pnkjGlassNoise(p*2.03+7.1)*0.3*detail+pnkjGlassNoise(p*4.01-3.7)*0.1*detail;}
void main(){vec2 u=acScreenNorm;vec2 p=u*scale+phase;float e=0.02;vec2 g=vec2(pnkjGlassFbm(p+vec2(e,0))-pnkjGlassFbm(p-vec2(e,0)),pnkjGlassFbm(p+vec2(0,e))-pnkjGlassFbm(p-vec2(0,e)))/(2.0*e);gl_FragColor=texture2DCv(inputImg.texture,clamp(u+g*amount,0.0,1.0));}

name: GM Volumetric Sweep
desc: Soft directional light volume controlled by center, width and falloff.
shader: const vec3 L=vec3(0.2126,0.7152,0.0722);void main(){vec2 u=acScreenNorm;vec2 c=(acLayerCenter-center*vec2(-1.0))/acScreenSize;vec2 d=vec2(cos(angle),sin(angle));vec2 q=u-c;float across=abs(dot(q,vec2(-d.y,d.x)));float forward=max(dot(q,d),0.0);float beam=exp(-pow(across/max(width,0.0001),2.0))*exp(-forward*falloff);vec4 s=texture2DCv(inputImg.texture,u);float gate=0.25+0.75*dot(s.rgb,L);gl_FragColor=vec4(s.rgb+lightColor.rgb*beam*strength*gate,s.a);}
